Weekly Digest: Leads Assemble, Polls Go Live, and Unreal Takes the Lead

Weekly Digest · Jun 21 – Jun 28, 2026 · 1509 messages from 49 members

What a week for the ASGC Game Jam! Between Jun 21 and Jun 28, two waves of leadership arrived, every discipline drafted its community poll, and the production team built the scaffolding that will hold up a 300+ person jam. Here's what happened, who made it happen, and what's still open.

The Leadership Team Takes Shape

On Mon Jun 22, GreenCat (Mila) welcomed Wave One, the Discipline Leads, in #🎸│general. Diana Donado is Creative Director and Sidds (shadowarrior) is Executive Producer. New arrivals were asked to:

  • match their server name to LinkedIn
  • read #rules and #faq
  • do the Day 0 tasks

Xelnath (Alex) set the naming format: FirstName LastName (Role) (Timezone), prefixed with a discipline emoji. He also set the succession rules: a departing lead nominates a replacement, and the leads vote by majority.

On Fri Jun 26 the second wave arrived. 'Feature Leads' were renamed Deputy Leads, so the structure is now 16 discipline leads, each with 2–4 deputies. NitsujyN (Justin) explained that deputies:

  • assist their discipline leads
  • act as the first line of support for participants
  • fill gaps where needed

He also confirmed the role can go on LinkedIn, and both answers were added to the FAQ. GreenCat automated role assignment (after 2 AM her time!).

On Saturday, about 20 leads introduced themselves in #🎯│leads-discussion. Their backgrounds include:

  • Epic (Mason, Adrian)
  • Rocket League (Matt Barnes)
  • For Honor (Novendar)
  • Final Fantasy VII QA (KyotoRando)
  • Gameloft, Wolcen and Roblox

Other notes: - Matt Barnes is covering Level Design until someone is promoted from within. - Swart Tigerhorn picked up UI/UX design. - Imraël (Sébastien) joined as Narrative Co-Lead alongside Leslie (Oldladies7). - Hailey (Bori) joined as Audio Co-Lead.

Role colors will be department roles in shades of Red/Blue. Oldladies7 also opened a poll on whether to keep the red/blue team system at all.

Day 0: Planting the Jam's Seed

In #Day 0 - Discussion - HERE, Xelnath set the task: each discipline submits one easy question with 5 options for a LinkedIn poll, so the community can choose the jam's 'seed'. His guidance:

  • Scope for 6 weeks, not 6 months.
  • Run the polls at the same time.
  • Embrace weird combinations as 'uncomfortable constraints'.

What each discipline drafted:

  • Narrative (Leslie and Imraël): genre, setting and theme polls, marked done Jun 23. The narrative pod will poll on genre tropes and build story themes around the winner.
  • Design (Matt Barnes): a genre list that grew into a broad core gameplay loop poll, which Xelnath approved.
  • Audio (exackley): a sonic-style poll with Cartoon/Playful, Hyper Realistic, Real, Fantasy and Arcade.
  • Other proposals came from QA (sabishi_angel), Art (Sabian), Tech (VibeBlind) and Production (Cafedunoir).

Matt suggested releasing polls one at a time to tame chaotic combos. Diana Donado urged simple lists and making the final pick together as a team. shadowarrior finalized the list in #Genre and Theme Poll Discussion on Jun 24.

Early frontrunners are Steampunk, Detective Thriller Mystery and Exploring New Worlds, with Mystery leading by about 50%. Amir's LinkedIn results are due to be announced to leads first.

Narrative team's two candidate polls: abstract themes vs. genre tropes — by Oldladies7 in #Genre and Theme Poll Discussion

Building the Production Machine

Sidds created most of the project's core docs:

  • the Gameplan Scratchpad
  • the Master Questionnaire
  • the Leads Contact Info sheet
  • a blocker-resolution flowchart

He ran the first Leads Sync on Jun 24. Michal Fried collected all of these, plus the Master QA Document and the sync notes, in #📚│lead-only-resources. She also explained the Drive layout: the main GameJam folder holds lead-only info, and participant-facing material goes in a separate folder.

In #🗓️│production-lead-discussion, the producers (Sidds, Lori/Cafedunoir and Daniel Beahn) agreed on:

  • ClickUp for the schedule and timeline
  • daily Miro checks for blockers
  • one weekly sync
  • an onboarding checklist

Lori drafted a 26-week milestone plan: Alpha 6, Beta 6, RC 6, GM 5 and Final 3. It may still change to account for holidays.

VibeBlind (Seth) proposed a weekly release cadence:

  • Sat–Mon: development
  • Tue: feature integration
  • Wed: branch freeze, bug fixes only
  • Thu: QA and release candidate
  • Fri: stable release

Lori floated Kanban instead of sprints. Xelnath clarified that the 'special limitation' task means 5 options that downscope, not upscope.

On tooling: ClickUp is free, but its GitHub integration is paid, so GitHub for Miro sync is a possible alternative. Leslie moved narrative tracking away from Notion because of its guest cap.

Alex's updated timeline dates for the leads. — by Xelnath in #🎯│director-discussion

Engine, Repo and Docs: The Technical Backbone

On Saturday in #🎯│leads-discussion, VibeBlind said the team will likely use Unreal, pending the Art Lead's confirmation and the poll results.

  • Support: Matt Barnes, klight and sokky cited industry and portfolio value.
  • Concerns: Alan and sokky raised hardware and disk space, and others asked about Paper2D.
  • Godot: the art team's lean toward 2D/low-poly, with only about 13 3D-focused art applicants out of roughly 400, revived the question.
  • Perforce: out of budget, and klight learned it has no license program for volunteer groups.

In #GitHub Repository Limits, Adrian flagged GitHub's free-tier limits: about 10GB of storage, a 2GB monthly LFS bandwidth cap and a 100MB per-file limit. He offered to self-host Gitea/GitLab with a public push mirror.

Xelnath set the key constraint: the source and assets must stay publicly served. VibeBlind listed the options: strict asset hygiene, crowdfunded LFS or external storage, or splitting the project across repos. Still unresolved.

Documentation now follows a three-way split agreed in #📄│design-lead-discussion and #💻│tech-lead-discussion:

  • GDD = why (Matt's template)
  • TDD = how (Swart Tigerhorn's Unreal Blueprint-based template, which opens with 'What is the problem we are solving?')
  • GitHub Issues = what, as bite-sized tasks

In #🪲│qa-lead-discussion, QA and Tech settled on GitHub Issues with bug templates. pulsegenerator found the Triage access level, and Hanhula granted VibeBlind GitHub org access.

klight's disk usage: Unity installs outweighing Unreal — by klight in #🎯│leads-discussion

GitHub docs screenshot showing read-only users can open issues — by Hanhula in #🪲│qa-lead-discussion

Where Each Discipline Stands on AI

In #Day-1-LLM Based Generation & Tools and in the discipline channels, leads answered three questions: is AI allowed for content, for tools, and for support work? The shared baseline is disclosure plus human review.

  • Art (Sabian and Diana): no AI final artwork. Limited AI is allowed for tools, scripting and tech art, and AI is fine for notes and summaries.
  • Tech (VibeBlind): yes to all three, with disclosure for content. Contributors must understand, be able to explain, and be able to maintain what they submit. Swart called AI detection a 'blind witch hunt.'
  • Design (Matt): AI is OK during iteration and for rough prototypes, but no AI content in the release.
  • Audio (exackley): AI is fine for docs and tech help. Content is most likely a no, unless the workload outgrows the team.
  • QA (pulsegenerator): AI can help with test cases and automation, but not with subjective testing like usability.
  • UI/UX (Swart): AI for text only, not visuals.

Xelnath noted that the decisions are locked in, but nobody is required to use AI.

Bridging the Disciplines

In #📝│narrative-lead-discussion, Leslie shared diagrams of the narrative workflow, decision hierarchy and production pipeline. pulsegenerator and sabishi_angel pushed to bring QA in early, checking tone, consistency and legal or cultural issues, not just spelling. The current proposal:

  • Each discipline gets a single QA point of contact.
  • QA reviews content before Leslie's final approval.

VibeBlind said writers can hand off Google Doc links instead of learning Git, and he plans 1:1s with every lead to work out handoffs. Swart Tigerhorn volunteered as the Tech–Narrative bridge.

AaronBurrSir offered production help to reduce duplicated effort across pods. Daniel suggested a full production-team discussion to hear his proposal.

Shoutouts

  • shadowarrior (Sidds) — Drove production. He built the Gameplan Scratchpad, Master Questionnaire, contact sheet and blocker flowchart, ran the first Leads Sync, and finalized the poll list.
  • VibeBlind (Seth) — Set the technical direction: proposed Unreal, a weekly release cadence, the GDD/TDD/Issue split and a soft-then-lock decision process. He also set up the GitHub workflows with QA.
  • GreenCat (Mila) — Welcomed both waves, automated role assignment after 2 AM her time, and gave Discipline Leads permission to create Discord Events.
  • Swart Tigerhorn — Built the Unreal Blueprint-based TDD template, reorganized the GDD, took on UI/UX design, and volunteered as the Tech–Narrative bridge.
  • Michal Fried — Turned #lead-only-resources into a well-organized hub of planning docs, set up the Drive structure, added an audio section to the Miro board, and shared a mobile-friendly timestamp tool.

Coming up: Amir's LinkedIn poll results, the Art Lead's call on Unreal, Matt's feature structure and documentation needs, due Monday, and Sidds' trimmed-down Master Questionnaire. Still open: how to host the repo so it stays free and public, Gitflow vs. trunk-based development, channel access for 30+ deputies, whether the red/blue teams survive the vote, and how to handle sprints over holidays. Public signups close 07/14. See you next week, and keep those toe splinters coming!
